The '''Zhensanovian Languages''' are the diverse language family of the [[Union of Zhensanov]]. Source material describes more than one hundred regional and sub-regional languages with loosely Slavic roots and a shared [[Proto-Zhensanovian]] ancestry.

== Federal Language Diversity ==

Zhensanovian linguistic diversity is a major part of the Union's cultural structure. The source describes the family as decentralized, with no single natural language dominating the whole Union. That diversity helps explain both federal identity and the pressure for later standardization.

The major source-named branches are [[Murianic Languages|Murianic]], [[Agashkinic Languages|Agashkinic]], [[Tekdolian Languages|Tekdolian]], [[Toramdic Languages|Toramdic]], and [[Kavetsian Languages|Kavetsian]].

== Writing Systems ==

Before modern standardization, Zhensanovian languages used several traditional writing systems, including runic, syllabic, modified Cyrillic-derived, pictographic, and regional systems. The [[Union Alphabet]] was later developed as a standardized script able to represent sounds across the language family.

This draft preserves the Union Alphabet as the 1994-back script-policy anchor. The later source claim that Sanovic became a constructed Union lingua franca belongs to the post-1994 pass, because the Sanovic source places its creation in the early twenty-first century.

== Naming And Identity ==

Source material links different naming conventions to different language branches: Murianic patronymics, Agashkinic clan endings, Tekdolian compound surnames, Toramdic dual names, and Kavetsian lineage titles. These conventions are useful cultural evidence but need a dedicated pass before being used for named characters or official regional histories.
